slides.texte_overlay:
How to stay calm
in a job interview
Prepare three stories, not thirty answers. One success, one failure you learned from, one time you helped a team. Almost every question can be answered with one of them.
Arrive fifteen minutes early, then walk around the block. You're never late, and you walk in calm instead of sitting in reception getting more nervous.
Pause before you answer. "Good question, let me think." A two-second pause sounds thoughtful and confident, not unsure. Rushed answers sound nervous.
Remember they want you to succeed. The interviewer needs to fill the role. They're hoping you're the right person, not trying to catch you out on anything.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A calm, curious mind makes you sound sharper and more relaxed in any interview.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A calm, curious mind makes you sharper in any interview.

slides.texte_overlay: Ask them good questions. "What does success look like in this role after six months?" It shows interest and turns the interview into a real conversation.
Treat it as practice, not a verdict. Every interview makes you better at the next one. Thinking this way takes the pressure off and lets your real self show.
